I'm just going to focus on textures, keep my comment simple, but two thoughts on streaming textures.

First is latency, if you're only downloading the higher res version of the textures when it's needed, there is a delay for download to start. I've seen avatars take up to 20 seconds to start loading, but maybe that's because of an API call. Still could be 2 second delay there.

Second is compression, the asset bundle is a bunch of data that gets compressed, and the algorithm looks at the whole pile and tries a bunch of things to compress it. Making it so that only part of the bundle needs to be downloaded to get certain resolutions would make things a bit inefficient.

I think it's okay to download full textures, and would like to see mipmap streaming actually used. Unload higher resolutions if there isn't enough VRAM

I wouldn't mind seeing music split off, as I always have avatar audio muted.

details:
I would love to see systems that would offer either static or real-time baking of assets for avatars.

Say for example you have an avatar that is a body, and on that body are multiple texture swaps. There may also be a variety of different clothing meshes and textures for those.

I believe that there should be a system in place where only the low resolution/quality versions of the textures are actually downloaded, and high quality textures can be streamed to the avatar (and this should only apply selectively, so that things like continuously animated textures do not waste bandwidth).

There should also be a system for either statically or dynamically baking meshes. For example, you could assign all of the clothing meshes of the avatar to a single mesh name, and when uploading the avatar, it can upload combinations of clothing as different meshes and stream the appropriate one to the client. Another way could be to bake the mesh in real-time at a cost to a potential performance hitch.

This can be combined with systems to bake *like* or *similar* materials, as if one object uses Standard Shader (or a merged mesh uses Standard Shader), you should be able to merge those materials together into a single material which contains all necessary textures to function. This might also require new components to be able to handle things like texture swapping due to the generation of a dynamic material.

The idea is that performance on customizeable avatars can be greatly reduced, by being able to bake stable states of the avatar to a much more graphically optimized format, and by being able to stream the bits and pieces of the avatar dynamically, so the entire avatar is not constantly loaded to disk or memory.

This can also come with a benefit of being able to statically compute performance ranking, such that each object that is already kept track of for streaming can apply negative performance impacts dynamically, resulting in avatars that can be Very Poor in one configuration, but Poor or less in another. This can allow avatars to swap dynamically between their fallback/impostor and current versions based on the current total performance impact based on all of the assets currently requested.

Blend shapes can also be merged in this scenario, such that blend shapes with the same name can be adjusted for all the meshes when merged to handle information such as different body shapes efficiently.
title: [Feature Request] Material and Mesh Baking
